title: Independent ideas. Extraordinary finds.
intro: A daily selection of independent games and useful Android apps, with original F7 insights and links to their creators.

entries.name: Source of Mana

price.label: Free, open-source (MIT-licensed code, permissively licensed content)

entries.summary: An open-source 2D MMORPG built on Godot 4 by veterans of The Mana World, chasing the feel of late-1990s pixel-art RPGs. The project is still in early development yet already offers a playable solo and multiplayer experience with a server-authoritative world, quests, monster combat and loot. Desktop, Android and browser clients are listed as targets of the same codebase, and the client, server, maps and credited art library are all public.
features: Godot 4 client and server with a dynamic, server-authoritative world you can read and run yourself
Quests, monster battles and loot collection in a pixel-art fantasy world mapped with Tiled
Desktop (Windows, macOS, Linux), Android and HTML5/WebAssembly clients named as platform targets
Labelled keyboard shortcuts for stats, skills, quests, minimap, chat and social panels, alongside click-to-move
MIT-licensed code with a separately credited CC BY-SA 4.0 art and sound list, so contributors can reuse assets lawfully
entries.insight: MMOs normally end the day their operator stops paying for servers. A world whose client, server and content are all under permissive licences can be re-hosted by the people who played it, which makes Source of Mana as much a preservation experiment as a role-playing game.

entries.name: Cave Express

price.label: Free, open-source (GPL-3.0-or-later code, CC BY-SA 4.0 assets)

entries.summary: A classic 2D platformer with physics-based gameplay: you master a pedal-powered flying machine, collect packages from cave-dwelling clients and drop them at the collection point while mastodons and pterodactyls object. The same repository also ships CavePacker, a sokoban puzzle game built from XSokoban, KSokoban, sasquatch, microban and gri* maps. Both games carry network multiplayer and a built-in map editor, and both are playable as official browser builds.
features: Box2D physics platforming across dozens of levels, with the map editor reachable from the main menu
CavePacker sokoban included, with its own editor and network-based multiplayer
Official Emscripten web builds of both games hosted on GitHub Pages
Windows, macOS, Linux and Android builds, an apt package in Debian, stable releases on GitHub and nightly CI artefacts
In-game console on Shift+Tab plus an optional runtime command pipe for scripting and headless debugging
entries.insight: Cave Express still ships the tools that produced its own level pool: the editor sits in the menu, the artwork is licensed for reuse, and the browser build means the shortest path from curiosity to playing is a single link rather than an installer.

entries.name: Rhythia
entries.summary: A free and open-source rhythm game in which notes arrive across a 3x3 grid and your mouse is the instrument. Formerly Sound Space Plus, it is being rebuilt in Godot 4.7 with C#, while the legacy Nightly client remains downloadable for new players. Beatmaps come from the community into a user folder, and the project is emphatic that it shares no connection with the commercial Steam title of the same name.
features: Mouse-driven play across a 3x3 grid rather than the usual lane keys
Rewrite client built with Godot 4.7 and C#, with Windows and Linux builds on GitHub Releases
Legacy Nightly client still published from the original sound-space-plus repository, with current development focused on the rewrite
Maps are distributed separately into a user folder, so communities can share their own beatmaps
AGPL-3.0 source, with the project explicitly supporting modification of its logos and content under that licence
entries.insight: A name collision with a commercial Steam rhythm game could have drowned this one. Instead, the README draws the boundary in a warning box, points players at the correct downloads and then invites people to remix its own artwork under the AGPL - a confident, unusual use of a copyleft licence.

entries.name: No Survivor Game
entries.summary: A three-act science-fiction survivors-like that runs entirely in a browser tab: a Godot 4 export delivered as WebAssembly, piloted with the mouse on desktop and a virtual joystick on phones. Each run mixes dual-element gunfire, enemy hardware you salvage mid-battle and rule-changing module cards. Unusually for the genre, the project publishes its own automated test results and states which claims those tests cannot support.
features: Three-act campaign of shattered orbit, storm front and mothership approach, with two shuffled regular bosses, an OMEGA finale and endless play after victory
Dual-element main fire where five elements produce ten pair reactions and a third element replaces a chosen slot
Six recoverable hardware types - cannons, mines, reflective armour, tractor equipment, tail bombers and splitters - that visibly attach to the wings
54 illustrated module cards with three rerolls per run, plus six rule modifications across two active slots
Twelve encounter patterns and six tactical support roles, with captured turrets that provide real covering fire
Save data and discovery history stay on the device, and controlled screenshots are labelled as staged rather than natural progression
entries.insight: The README admits what its own checks cannot prove: no phone thermals, no balance data, no player-retention evidence, and screenshots that are staged engine captures. In a genre marketed almost entirely through highlight reels, publishing the limits of your evidence is a distinctive form of design discipline.

entries.name: Togetherness Table

price.label: Free, open-source (AGPL-3.0), self-host or use a public demo

entries.summary: A web virtual tabletop built around one decision: the session is an SVG document. Players move toys, draw and edit shapes and author rules and behaviours inside that shared document, which syncs peer-to-peer while the signalling server only brokers WebRTC handshakes and never sees content. There are no accounts and no canonical server copy, so documents persist in IndexedDB, keep working offline and merge when peers reconnect.
features: The entire game state lives in one shared SVG document you can save to disk and edit in tools such as Inkscape
Peer-to-peer CRDT synchronisation, with a signalling server that never receives document content
No accounts, no server-side storage and no build step: clone the repository, run one command and open a browser
Offline-first persistence through IndexedDB, with sync resuming automatically when peers return
Real-time join by sharing a URL hash, tested with Playwright end-to-end against a full app and signalling stack
entries.insight: Virtual tabletops are the subscription product most exposed to shutdown, because your campaign lives in their database. Making the canvas an ordinary SVG file with local-first sync is the technical answer to a very human worry, and it is stated as a goal: survival post-demise.

asset.attribution: Togetherness Table wordmark from the sjbrown/togetherness repository, reproduced unmodified under the project's AGPL-3.0 licence.

entries.name: Neon Mayhem

price.label: Free in the browser, with no install, account or ads

entries.summary: A neon open world set in Costa Rosa in 1986 that plays from a browser tab: steal a ride, outrun the heat, take a job or buy a condo with the takings, or cruise the beachfront at night with the radio on. It is written in plain JavaScript on three.js with no build step, so it runs from any static host, and all music and sound are synthesised at runtime with the Web Audio API. This fan-made tribute states that no assets from the game that inspired it are used.
features: Two islands linked by bridges you earn, with enterable shops, a casino with horse racing, a glass car showroom and homes you can buy
Six stars of heat answered by roadblocks, spike strips, harbour launches, a searchlight helicopter and, at the top level, the army
Sports cars, bikes, a limo, an ice-cream truck, a monster truck, a tank, a helicopter, a looping plane, speedboats, a jet ski and swimming
Street races, couriers, rampages, takedowns, taxi and ambulance shifts and story jobs, plus 35 stunt jumps and 30 hidden mixtapes
Three radio stations with a fourth to find, every note synthesised live in the browser with the Web Audio API
Keyboard, controller and touch layouts, with progress saved in the browser and classic cheat codes entered by list or button combo
entries.insight: The engineering constraint is the appeal: no downloaded media, no build step and audio synthesised at runtime, so a whole crime-sandbox city exists as source you could host yourself. It is a concrete answer to how much of an open world code can carry.

asset.attribution: Neon Mayhem screenshot of a four-star police chase at night, from the pranshuparmar/neon-mayhem repository, reproduced unmodified under the project's Apache-2.0 licence. The project states everything in it is original work and that no assets from the game that inspired it are used; it is a fan-made tribute, not affiliated with or endorsed by Rockstar Games or Take-Two Interactive.

entries.name: Redocted
entries.summary: A daily guessing game played on a page of AWS or Kubernetes documentation with most of its words blacked out. Every guess is revealed wherever it appears, and you win by uncovering all of the title. Word matching happens in the browser against a committed corpus, a new puzzle lands at 00:00 UTC for everyone, older puzzles stay playable and an endless mode serves random articles without touching your streak.
features: Two daily boards, AWS and Kubernetes, built from documentation excerpts of at most 700 words with a link back to each source page
Morphological matching with no shipped dictionary, so policy reveals policies while look-alikes such as plan and plane stay apart
Hints reveal the word with the most matches first, never a title word, and never count as guesses
Tap a black bar for its letter count, enable counts permanently, or rely on screen-reader announcements of every hidden word's length
Result card with accuracy, guesses and hints used, plus spoiler-free sharing to X, Bluesky, LinkedIn, WhatsApp or Telegram
Interface in English and Portuguese, with a separate Portuguese board and a browser-only endless mode
entries.insight: Vendor documentation is about the driest reading available, which is exactly why the puzzle works: it turns a few thousand pages of cloud reference into a daily vocabulary drill in the specific language people are paid to understand.

entries.name: QuickBuds

price.label: Free, open-source (GPL-3.0-or-later), with optional Ko-fi support

entries.summary: An open-source companion for OnePlus, OPPO and realme earbuds that replaces HeyMelody and realme Link by talking to already-paired buds and showing only the controls your model actually has. Android gets home-screen widgets and Quick Settings tiles, desktop gets a tray panel, and the model database is published with owner confirmations recorded per device. It is a hobby project that can outlive the vendor apps it substitutes.
features: Covers all 140 models in the HeyMelody and realme Link lists, with 49 confirmed working by owners
Adaptive feature surface: ANC, EQ, high-quality audio, 3D audio, low-latency mode, gesture remapping, find-my-earbud and hearing and fit tests, shown only where supported
Home-screen widgets, Quick Settings tiles and a battery notification on Android; a system-tray panel on Windows and Linux
Android 8 or later, Windows 10 and 11 from a no-installer zip, and x64 Linux on any distribution, all from GitHub Releases, named as the only official downloads
Interface in 27 languages with four styles and many themes, updating itself from GitHub releases
A published SHA-256 signing-certificate fingerprint so an APK from elsewhere can be checked for genuineness
entries.insight: Earbud features disappear whenever a vendor rewrites its companion app or a phone stops shipping it. QuickBuds documents the reverse-engineered protocol and keeps per-model owner confirmations, which is what turns a hobby alternative into infrastructure people can rely on after the official app is abandoned.

distribution.label: Official GitHub Releases (Android APK, Windows and Linux builds)

entries.name: mpvium
entries.summary: An Android front end for libmpv that keeps the engine's flexibility and wraps it in a Material 3 interface with real media browsing and network sources. The stated philosophy is sane defaults with pro-level control, and the reasoning behind those defaults is written down rather than left to guesswork. Preview builds ship from GitHub Releases as universal and per-architecture APKs.
features: Hardware-accelerated playback through libmpv, with picture-in-picture and background playback
One-tap intro and recap skipping with a countdown chip and an offline cache of detected markers
Gesture controls, zoom and orientation controls, plus chapters, playlists, playback history and resume
Local browsing in folder and tree views, with network playback over SMB, FTP and WebDAV
Custom mpv configuration, script support and advanced playback options when the defaults are not enough
External subtitles and audio tracks, metadata caching, and no advertisements or unnecessary permissions
entries.insight: mpv is famously powerful and famously awkward on a phone. mpvium's contribution is the layer between: it keeps config files and scripts reachable while encoding its judgement in a written doctrine, so a new user inherits sensible behaviour instead of an empty text file.

entries.name: Z-Sync
entries.summary: A companion app for Zen Browser that carries its space-based workflow to a phone. It syncs spaces, tabs and essentials over Firefox Sync, accepts links shared from other apps into a chosen space as a pinned or ordinary tab, and opens follow-up lookups in a small built-in browser so you never leave the list. Native Kotlin and Compose on Android, SwiftUI on iOS, maintained by one developer.
features: Syncs Zen Browser spaces, tabs and essentials through Firefox Sync, with a published sync contract and golden fixtures in the repository
Share-sheet integration saves a link into a chosen space as a pinned tab or a normal tab
Quick in-app browser for lookups without leaving the current space
Bundled EasyList and EasyPrivacy blocking plus DuckDuckGo autoconsent for cookie banners
Native clients on both platforms: Kotlin with Jetpack Compose, and SwiftUI generated with XcodeGen
Free and ad-free, MIT-licensed, with Zen-derived icons kept separately under MPL-2.0
entries.insight: Vertical-tab workspaces fixed desktop browsing and quietly abandoned the phone, where tab sprawl is worst. Z-Sync bets that a workspace is worth carrying around and that Firefox Sync is already the plumbing for it - a small app filling a gap the browser vendors left open.

entries.name: Petal

price.label: Free (GPL-3.0), with GitHub, Google Play and F-Droid builds

entries.summary: An Android browser built on Mozilla GeckoView 159 rather than the system WebView, which is what lets it install genuine Firefox add-ons from AMO or a .xpi file. Blocking runs through a bundled WebExtension fed by EasyList, uBlock Origin uAssets and Hagezi lists alongside Gecko's strict tracking protection, and optional encrypted sync works through a folder you own.
features: GeckoView 159 with Mozilla Android Components, so rendering and extension APIs match desktop Firefox
Firefox WebExtensions support: add-on manager, AMO installs, .xpi import and ten built-in extensions
Built-in petal_network_blocker using EasyList, uBlock Origin uAssets and Hagezi lists, with Enhanced Tracking Protection on Strict by default
Optional encrypted sync of bookmarks, history, passwords and tabs through a folder you control, plus Send to device
100 percent Kotlin 2.4 with Jetpack Compose and Material 3 Expressive, on Android 8.0 and newer, with 28 translations
Builds on GitHub with an in-app updater, on Google Play, and on F-Droid without ads or Google code
entries.insight: Most Android browsers marketed on privacy are WebView skins with a filter list. Shipping a Firefox engine is a far larger maintenance promise, but it is the only route to real add-ons - which is why Petal can run the blocker itself rather than imitate one.

distribution.label: Official GitHub Releases with in-app updater

entries.name: XGesture
entries.summary: A system-level gesture and one-hand productivity suite for Android 12 and newer, built on accessibility services rather than firmware so Samsung, Xiaomi, Pixel and everything else behave the same. Behind the edge swipes sits an offline text and image toolkit - OCR, translation, search aggregation and reverse image search - that reads what is on screen without a cloud round trip.
features: Multi-angle screen-edge triggers mapped to 50+ system actions, with dedicated landscape handles, animations and per-app anti-mistouch rules
Reachability floating cursor, multi-function floating ball, and shake, desk-flip and back-tap triggers
On-device OCR through ML Kit, Tesseract and PaddleOCR ONNX, offered as a full build with bundled engines or a compact lite build
Text selection panel for translate, copy and search, plus multi-engine reverse image search with an in-app preview
Notification and OTP managers, app freezer, widget overlays and freeform windows adapted to MIUI, HyperOS and Flyme small windows
Optional Shizuku, Root or KernelSU or Magisk, and LSPosed privilege modes, with Obtainium installing updates from GitHub Releases
entries.insight: OEM gesture suites are firmware features that vanish the moment you change brands. Rebuilding that layer as accessibility services with optional elevated privileges means the muscle memory survives the phone upgrade, which explains why its documentation is written around hand positions rather than features.

entries.name: Femto Car Launcher

price.label: Free, open-source (Apache-2.0); the optional Google Maps provider bills your own key

entries.summary: An Android home launcher that replaces the screen with a single fixed dashboard designed for automotive viewing distances and touch accuracy: a live map fills the display while driving data, weather, calendar and media sit in glanceable panels. It targets aftermarket CarPlay and Android Auto boxes, Android head units and dash-mounted phones, and it records trips entirely on the device.
features: Live map behind the interface, using a keyless OpenStreetMap provider through OpenFreeMap or a Google Maps provider with your own API key
Heading-up navigation camera with easing, a compass toggle to north-up, detachable panning, and optional 3D buildings and terrain relief
Speed overlay with trip distance, average speed, altitude and reverse-geocoded address, GPX export and a 3D wireframe flythrough of recorded tracks
Weather from the Norwegian Meteorological Institute with offline caching, a device-calendar strip, and now-playing controls for any media session
An optional video window over the map whose picture stays hidden until GPS reads the vehicle as stopped, while audio keeps playing
Android 13 and newer, stable and nightly APKs on GitHub Releases, with dashboard screenshots kept as CI screenshot-test references
entries.insight: Car screens are usually served by phone apps scaled up. Femto treats the dashboard as the launcher itself - one screen, no app switching - and pins its look to screenshot tests that block a pull request when the interface drifts, which is how a hobby project keeps a glanceable UI honest.

entries.name: AFinity

price.label: Free, open-source (GPL-3.0); requires your own Jellyfin server

entries.summary: A native Android client for Jellyfin 12, written in Kotlin and Jetpack Compose with libmpv for playback, that goes well past streaming: live TV with a guide, Audiobookshelf books and podcasts, community subtitle discovery, and title requests through Seerr. Everything beyond Jellyfin is opt-in per server and per profile, and the privacy section states plainly that nothing is tracked or analysed.
features: libmpv-backed playback of movies, shows, music and live TV with multiple audio, subtitle and version selection and trickplay previews
Home screen rows you reorder, hide or build from a library, genre, studio, collection, playlist or filter, including franchise grouping and ranked IMDb Top 250 rows
Audiobookshelf integration for audiobooks and podcasts, with Audible ratings fetched on book pages
Online subtitle search through your server's plugins and TheSubtitleDB, tagged for hearing-impaired and AI-generated tracks
Media requests via Seerr and per-server opt-in for MDBList, TMDB, OMDb, Last.fm and Wikidata
Requires Jellyfin 12.0 and Android 15 or newer, with GPL-3.0 source, no analytics and update checks off until enabled
entries.insight: Jellyfin's official apps have long trailed the server's own capabilities, so the community keeps building better front ends. AFINITY is interesting for how it resists growth: every external metadata source stays off until you enable it, and its privacy page names the exact identifier each service receives.
